newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey preparing medium-term stability programme.
newsitem.headline: Turkey preparing medium-term stability programme.

text.p: Turkey is studying a medium-term stabilisation programme to lower chronic inflation to a single-digit level, state minister Ufuk Soylemez said.
"Our government is preparing a plan to lower inflation to 10 or nine percent over a period of three years," the semi-official Anatolian news agency quoted Soylemez as saying.
Soylemez, responsible for the Treasury and privatisation, said the Treasury and the central bank set up a technical committee to draw up the programme.

Central bank officials confirmed that the bank was working on a medium-term programme aimed at lowering inflation running at around 80 percent and drying up the sources of public deficits, estimated at more than 10 percent of the country's gross national product.
Soylemez and officials gave no details of the programme.
Bankers say the government is expected to unveil details of the programme ahead of talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) which Soylemez said would be held in late March or early April.

The IMF is expected to urge Turkey to take structural measures to improve taxation, reform loss-making pension system, speed up privatisation, narrow budget deficit and ease burden of domestic debt stock.
